summary.headline: Aurionpro Q2 FY27 revenue crossed INR 415 crore (up 16% YoY and QoQ) with EBITDA margin 17.2% and PAT margin 12%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a first-ever quarterly high of INR 415 crore, up 16% both YoY and QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 71 crore (17.2% margin) and PAT of INR 50 crore (12% margin). Management said R&D front-loading peaked in H1 and will moderate, while data center growth is expected to dilute enterprise margins. Working capital pressure rose: current borrowings went to about INR 150 crore from about INR 50 crore in March, and cash fell to about INR 83 crore, which management attributed to large data center contracts. Management declined to resume revenue guidance but said H2 would be stronger than H1.

financial_highlights.value: more than INR 2,000 crore (about INR 2,050 crore per analyst)

financial_highlights.change: up from about INR 50 crore in March 2026

segments.name: Banking and fintech
segments.commentary: Management said H1 was very strong and margins are at or slightly above expectations. First trade finance product launched, with another expected in Q3 or early Q4; several large deals in advanced stages and multiple POCs across Asia and Europe.

segments.name: Technology Innovation Group (transit and data center)
segments.commentary: Data center is roughly two-thirds of TIG order book in combination with banking at one-third, and is north of 30% of total order book. Data center revenue is estimated at 40-50% of TIG revenue this year versus about one-third last year; management expects data center to grow 70-80% or more this year.

segments.name: Transit
segments.commentary: Management said margins have been trending up and will improve slightly into H2. Finland win marks Nordic entry, with more European and US opportunities targeted.

segments.name: Data center
segments.commentary: New contracts are contributing a little revenue so far, but cost is ahead of revenue; margins are below enterprise levels for now. Billing and contractual issues weighed on H1 unbilled revenue and cash.

guidance_outlook: Management will not give revenue guidance, citing uncertainty and that a company of its size should not do so.
Enterprise EBITDA margin expected in a 17-18% band for FY27 and FY28, per the CEO's answer to a follow-up; management said it would revisit at Q3 if there is a meaningful change.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1, with no quantification given.
Collections expected to skew to Q3 and Q4; OCF-to-EBITDA of 60-70% described as doable.
R&D intensity expected to moderate after H1 peak; management has not added development headcount for several quarters.
Expects to ship new AI-native software every quarter this year and to announce banking wins in Q3 and Q4.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation of R&D fell in H1 as major AI-native rebuilds (for example Verdict, Infinity OS, Lexsi Labs) near completion; capitalisation will continue at a lower level, mainly for payments business.
Data center delivery is capacity-constrained; management said building capacity on time is the key variable for converting revenue.
Plans to integrate backward into manufacturing critical components for data centers and mass transit; management described this as several quarters to years away.
Plans to set up in-house infrastructure for internal AI models over the next couple of quarters, with higher infra spend.
demand_pricing: Banking demand is recovering after Middle East and geopolitical delays; management expects significant Middle East wins within one or two quarters.
Order book of more than INR 2,000 crore; about 70-75% executable over the next 4-6 quarters, or at least 70% over four to five quarters.
AMCs and most recurring revenue are excluded from the order book.
Data center project timelines are shrinking to 12-18 months from longer gestation periods, adding pressure on delivery.
Management expects coding model prices to fall, not rise, reducing AI token cost risk.
Cybersecurity practice set up four quarters ago; revenue not yet material.

qa_highlights.question: What margin range should be underwritten for H2 FY27, and how much improvement comes from lower R&D versus operating leverage and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects enterprise margins to stay roughly at current levels; banking and transit margins to improve slightly in H2, offset by data center mix. Later confirmed 17-18% band for FY27 and FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is executable and how does H2 compare with H1?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% executable over 4-6 quarters, at least 70% over four to five quarters. No H2 growth quantification, but H2 described as much stronger than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise and cash fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to one or two large data center contracts that need retooling to deliver; expected to ease by year-end, with no significant long-run cash pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company resume guidance and what is the data center revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance, as a company of this size should not give it. Data center is about 40-50% of TIG revenue this year versus one-third last year; sub-segment revenue not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for OCF-to-EBITDA and unbilled revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: OCF-to-EBITDA of 60-70% described as doable with H2 collections skewed to Q3-Q4. Unbilled revenue overall close to last year's level; data center billing issues to be under control in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and revenue recognition profile on data center projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is somewhat high in H1 but not significant relative to project profit; revenue recognised progressively on 12-14 month projects, with billing kinks being worked out.

risks_watch: Working capital and cash: borrowings up, cash down, unbilled revenue and receivables high; data center billing issues.
Data center capacity build-out and delivery timelines may limit revenue conversion and margins.
Enterprise margin dilution from data center mix; management says margins stay around current levels.
Middle East decision cycles and geopolitical headwinds on banking deal timing.
Whether H2 R&D capitalisation truly falls and whether new investment is needed for transit global expansion.
Watch for unbilled revenue disclosure, data center separate segment reporting, and Q3 margin commentary.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term opportunity, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term cash, unbilled revenue and specific numbers (declined to quantify H2 growth, unbilled revenue and data center revenue). Management openly acknowledged a cash and billing struggle on large data center contracts.
key_quotes: Crossing quarterly revenue threshold for the first time ever establishes a strong baseline for the quarters ahead.
I think something between 60% and 70% is doable, and I think that's what we will sort of stay focused on.
I don't think there is any player of our size. I mean, you or any of the investors can educate me if you need to, but we looked at this across the market.
To be very transparent, a bit of struggle in terms of controlling the cash and unbilled side, but that is well under control in Q3, and we expect H2 to be very, very strong on that side.

growth.why: Numeric revenue guidance was withdrawn; management says H2 FY27 will be "a lot stronger" than H1 (unquantified), backed by an order book of over INR 2,000 crore with 70-75% executable in 4-6 quarters, but no specific capacity additions were quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Enterprise EBITDA margin guided in a 17-18% band for FY27-28 versus 17.2% in Q2, with banking and transit margins improving slightly in H2 but data center mix dilutive, so expansion is limited.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Data center delivery is capacity-constrained and building capacity on time is the key conversion variable, but no specific new capacity was quantified or dated.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management says H2 will be a lot stronger than H1 (H1 revenue base after Q2 at INR 415 crore, +16% YoY), backed by an order book above INR 2,000 crore with 70-75% executable over 4-6 quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Plans for in-house AI infrastructure over the next couple of quarters with higher infra spend, and backward integration into manufacturing is several quarters to years away; no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Numeric revenue guidance was withdrawn and management declined to resume it, so no formal upgrade path is set.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Data center billing and cash issues, capacity-constrained delivery and 12-18 month shrinking timelines pressure conversion, and management will revisit margins at Q3 if there is a meaningful change.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: every quarter, Q3 and Q4 FY27
rows.why: Management expects to ship new AI-native software every quarter this year and a second trade finance product in Q3 or early Q4 after the first launch.

rows.label: Collections skew to Q3-Q4; OCF-to-EBITDA 60-70%
rows.why: Current borrowings rose to about INR 150 crore from about INR 50 crore in March and cash fell to about INR 83 crore, with management guiding 60-70% OCF-to-EBITDA on H2 collections.

rows.label: Middle East and banking wins
rows.why: Management expects significant Middle East banking wins within one or two quarters and announcements of banking wins in Q3 and Q4 after delays from geopolitical headwinds.

rows.label: R&D intensity moderation
rows.why: R&D front-loading peaked in H1 with no development headcount added for several quarters, while capitalisation falls to a lower level mainly for payments.

tone.note: Management was confident on banking demand, data center opportunity and the 17-18% enterprise margin band, but cautious and evasive on cash, unbilled revenue and quantifying H2; analysts pushed on margin mix, working capital and guidance withdrawal.
